items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: the angle measured downward from the horizontal to a line of sight. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Explain why all four sloping edges of a right square-based pyramid are equal.
items.answer: The apex is directly above the centre, which is the same distance from all four corners; with the same height, Pythagoras gives equal edges.
items.markingKey: The apex is directly above the centre, which is the same distance from all four corners; with the same height, Pythagoras gives equal edges. (R1 R1)

items.stem: Explain why cos 70° = sin 20°.
items.answer: In a right-angled triangle the two acute angles add to 90°; the side adjacent to 70° is opposite 20°, so the two ratios are the same fraction.
items.markingKey: In a right-angled triangle the two acute angles add to 90°; the side adjacent to 70° is opposite 20°, so the two ratios are the same fraction. (R1 R1)

items.stem: Explain why cos⁻¹(21/18) gives an error on a calculator.
items.answer: cos of an angle in a right-angled triangle is adjacent/hypotenuse ≤ 1; the ratio here is greater than 1.
items.markingKey: cos of an angle in a right-angled triangle is adjacent/hypotenuse ≤ 1; the ratio here is greater than 1. (R1 A1)

items.stem: From the top of a lighthouse the angle of depression of a boat is 23°. Explain why the angle of elevation of the lighthouse top from the boat is also 23°, using a diagram description.
items.markingKey: The horizontal at the top and the sea level are parallel (R1); the line of sight is a transversal, so the angles are alternate and equal (R1).

items.stem: Explain why the space diagonal of a 3 × 6 × 3 cuboid equals √(3² + 6² + 3²).
items.answer: Base diagonal² = 3² + 6² (Pythagoras); space diagonal² = base diagonal² + 3² (Pythagoras again).
items.markingKey: Base diagonal² = 3² + 6² (Pythagoras); space diagonal² = base diagonal² + 3² (Pythagoras again). (R1 R1)

items.stem: Aiko writes: "sin 60° = sin 30° × 2 because 60 = 2 × 30." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Trig functions are not linear: sin 60° ≈ 0.866 but 2 sin 30° = 1.
items.markingKey: Trig functions are not linear: sin 60° ≈ 0.866 but 2 sin 30° = 1. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: In a right-angled triangle, the opposite side is 16 cm and the hypotenuse is 17 cm. Find the angle θ to 1 decimal place.
A kite string is 37 m long and makes an angle of elevation of 24°. Find the height of the kite.
items.markingKey: Correct diagram with the angle from the horizontal (M1); correct ratio (M1); 15 m (A1).

items.stem: A box is 10 cm long, 8 cm wide and 9 cm high. Find the angle between the space diagonal and the base.
items.markingKey: Base diagonal √(10² + 8²) (M1); second right-angled triangle (M1); 35.1° (A1).

items.stem: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 5 cm and an angle of 22°. Find the side adjacent to this angle.
items.markingKey: Correct ratio chosen (M1); 4.64 cm (A1).

items.stem: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 12 cm. Find the side adjacent to the 35° angle.
items.markingKey: Correct ratio (cos) (M1); correct rearrangement (M1); 9.83 cm (A1).

items.stem: A student claims that the angle of depression is measured from the vertical. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: It is measured from the horizontal, downwards.
items.markingKey: It is measured from the horizontal, downwards. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A cuboid measures 2 cm by 3 cm by 6 cm. Find the length of its space diagonal.
items.answer: 7 cm
items.markingKey: Base diagonal √(2² + 3²) (M1); second right-angled triangle (M1); 7 cm (A1).

items.stem: Given sin θ = 5/13 for an acute angle θ, find cos θ and tan θ exactly without a calculator, and verify that sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
items.markingKey: Correct missing side by Pythagoras or similarity (M1 A1); ratios formed (A1); verification/explanation complete (R1). cos θ = 12/13, tan θ = 5/12; (25 + 144)/169 = 1

items.stem: A ladder 3.25 m long leans against a wall. Its foot is 1.3 m from the wall. Find the angle with the ground and how far up the wall it reaches.
items.markingKey: Correct right-angled triangle(s) identified (M1); ratio(s) set up (M1 A1); answer 66.4°; 2.98 m (A1); conclusion/units in context (C1).

items.stem: Lars hikes 17 km on a bearing of 090° and then 13 km on a bearing of 180°. (a) How far is she from her starting point? (b) On what bearing must she walk to return directly to the start?
items.markingKey: Right angle between the legs identified (R1); distance by Pythagoras 21.4 km (M1 A1); angle at start by tan (M1); return bearing 307° (A1).

items.stem: A tent is a square-based pyramid with base 2 m and height 2.4 m. Find the slant height of a triangular face and the total area of canvas for the four faces.
items.answer: slant 2.6 m; canvas 10.4 m²
items.markingKey: Correct 2D right-angled triangle(s) extracted (M1 M1); Pythagoras/trig applied (A1 A1); answer with units and accuracy (C1). slant 2.6 m; canvas 10.4 m²
